title: Calm Calendar — free Google Calendar app for Windows, in 13 languages
meta_description: Calm Calendar is a free, ad-free desktop app for Google Calendar on Windows 10 and 11: day, week, month and schedule views, a desktop widget, quick add from any app, several accounts. Available in 13 languages.
og_title: Calm Calendar — Google Calendar for Windows
og_description: A free Google Calendar app for Windows, without ads, in 13 languages.
og_image_alt: Calm Calendar week view with colored events
lang_suggest: This site is available in English
hero_icon_alt: Calm Calendar app icon: a calendar with a leaf in the corner
hero_lead: A free, ad-free desktop calendar for Windows that shows your Google Calendar in day, week, month and schedule views, with a desktop widget and quick add from any app.
hero_shot_alt: Calm Calendar window showing a week view with a sidebar of calendars and colored events for each day
features_lead: Your Google Calendar in a native Windows window, without ads.
feature_p_1: Your Google Calendar in a fast native window. Drag events to move or resize them; repeats, guests and time zones included.
feature_p_2: Clock, a countdown to your next event, a mini month and upcoming events right on the desktop.
feature_p_3: Press Ctrl+Alt+Space anywhere, type “tomorrow 7pm gym 50 min” and press Enter. Understands all 13 languages of the app.
feature_p_4: A Join button for Google Meet, Zoom and Teams, and an optional alert over all windows when a meeting starts.
feature_p_5: Work and personal Google accounts in one window, with clashes between them marked. Add class schedules or Outlook calendars by their .ics link.
feature_p_6: Ctrl+K for any command, arrows to move between events, E to edit, Ctrl+D to duplicate. Press ? for the full list.
feature_p_7: Classic, Paper, Obsidian, Showcase or Monochrome, with a choice of fonts. The widget follows the style.
feature_p_8: Your Google Calendar reminders as Windows notifications.
feature_p_9: Shows the last loaded schedule when you have no connection.
feature_p_10: The app has no servers of its own, shows no ads and does not track you. Your data goes only between your PC and Google.
widget_alt: Calm Calendar desktop widget with a clock, a countdown to the next event, a mini month calendar and a list of upcoming events
languages_lead: Menus, dates, the tray and quick add are translated into all of them.
google_data_title: How Calm Calendar uses your Google data
google_data_intro: Calm Calendar signs in with your Google account and asks for two calendar permissions:
scope1_title: See the list of your calendars
scope1_desc: to show your calendars with their names and colors and let you hide or show each one.
scope2_title: View and edit events on your calendars
scope2_desc: to show your events and to create, edit, move and delete events when you do so in the app, and to show reminder notifications.
google_data_email: Sign-in also shares your Google account email address, so the app can show which account you are signed in with.
google_data_privacy_note: Everything runs on your computer. The app talks directly to Google; we never receive, store or share your data. You can sign out or remove access at any time.

faq_a_1: Yes. Calm Calendar is free and has no ads.
faq_a_2: Windows 10 version 1809 or later, and Windows 11.
faq_a_3: Partly. Calm Calendar is made for Google Calendar, but you can add an Outlook calendar, or any other, by its .ics link in Settings → Calendar subscriptions. Such calendars are read only.
faq_q_4: Which languages is the app in?
faq_a_4: English, Spanish, Portuguese, French, German, Russian, Ukrainian, Belarusian, Chinese, Japanese, Hindi, Bengali and Arabic. The app follows the Windows language, or you can pick one in Settings → Language.
faq_q_5: Can I use more than one Google account?
faq_a_5: Yes. Add as many accounts as you need; their calendars are shown together, and a meeting that clashes with another account's event is marked.
